Build a spatial_fit object for a backend of your own

Source: R/model-classes.R
new_spatial_fit.Rd

The constructor for the spatial_fit class, and the way to plug a model backend of your own into this package. The three built-in fitters (fit_rf_model(), fit_gwr_model() and fit_bayesian_spatial_model()) all end by calling it, and so should a custom fit_fn written for cv_spatial(). A model wrapped in a spatial_fit works with the package's folds, metrics, comparisons and area of applicability unchanged.

Usage

new_spatial_fit(
  subclass,
  engine,
  formula,
  response_var,
  predictor_vars,
  data_sf,
  info = list()
)

Arguments

subclass

Character scalar naming the class to stamp on the object: one of the built-ins "gwr_fit", "bayesian_fit" or "rf_fit", or any name of your own for a custom backend (say "lm_fit"). It is the S3 dispatch key: predict(), fitted(), residuals() and coef() on the result all dispatch on it, so a custom subclass needs a matching predict.<subclass>() method before cv_spatial() can use it.

engine

The raw model object your backend produced (an lm, a ranger object, a brmsfit, ...). Nothing inspects it except your own methods.

formula

A formula: the model, as print() and summary() show it. Its left side, when it has one, holds response_var (log(price) ~ elev for "price"). Its right side uses the columns predictor_vars names and no other attribute column of data_sf than these and the response, read by all.vars(), so log(elev) and elev * slope count as their columns, and so do the columns of an offset() or a grouping term; names that are not columns of data_sf and the reserved names ..x and ..y are not checked, and a right side with . is not read. A column a fit_fn derives itself and keeps out of predictor_vars, such as coordinates x and y for a trend surface, needs a name that is not a column of data_sf: on a layer that keeps its coordinates as columns x and y, derive them as cx and cy, or drop those columns first.

response_var

Character(1): the name of the response column of data_sf, an attribute column (not the geometry).

predictor_vars

Character vector of attribute column names of data_sf, not including response_var: the columns the right side of formula uses. character(0) for a model without predictors.

data_sf

An sf object with its geometry column: the rows the model was fitted on, with their geometry, in the order fitted() returns its values.

info

Named list of model-specific extras (list() for none). Set fitted_are_oob = TRUE when your fitted() values are held out instead of in-sample, so summary() labels them correctly.

Value

An object of class c(subclass, "spatial_fit"): a list with engine, formula, response_var, predictor_vars and data_sf as given, n (the number of rows of data_sf) and info (the list given, with a private cache environment added as info$.cache, which methods should not modify).

Details

A custom backend needs three things:

  1. a fit_fn that returns an object built by new_spatial_fit();

  2. a predict.<subclass>() method for the subclass you chose. cv_spatial() scores each fold by calling the predict() generic on the fit, so without one every fold fails;

  3. a fitted.<subclass>() method that returns one value per row of the fit's data_sf, in the same order. summary() and model_metrics() need it, and without one they stop with an error that names the method to define.

residuals() and coef() methods are optional.

The constructor checks the fields the package's functions read from a fit, and stops with an error that names the argument: subclass must be one class name, data_sf an sf object with its geometry column, formula a formula whose left side, when it has one, holds the response, response_var the name of one attribute column of data_sf (a column other than its geometry), predictor_vars a character vector of its attribute columns other than the response, the columns the right side of formula uses, and info a list. It does not check the response's type (a Bayesian fit can have a factor or ordinal response); summary() and model_metrics() refuse a response that is not numeric or logical.

The coef() contract

coef() on one of the three built-in backends either returns the coefficients or signals an error. It never returns NULL. A custom subclass inherits stats::coef.default(), which returns NULL, so define a coef.<subclass>() that errors when your backend has no coefficients. coef.rf_fit() always errors, because a forest has no coefficients; coef.gwr_fit() and coef.bayesian_fit() error when the backend cannot supply them (a missing package, an engine without the expected component). A NULL return could not be told from "this model has no fixed effects", and lapply(fits, coef) would return a shorter answer than the caller expected. Wrap the call in try() or tryCatch() when sweeping over a list of fits from different backends.

See also

cv_spatial(), which takes a custom fit_fn; fit_rf_model() for a built-in fitter.

Other model fitting: fit_bayesian_spatial_model(), fit_gwr_model(), fit_rf_model(), gp_lengthscale_bounds()

Examples

library(sf)
set.seed(1)
n <- 80
site <- st_as_sf(
  data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000),
             elev = rnorm(n)),
  coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632
)
site$price <- 10 + 0.01 * (st_coordinates(site)[, 1] - 5e5) +
  2 * site$elev + rnorm(n)

# A custom backend: an ordinary linear model behind the spatial_fit interface.
lm_fit <- function(train_sf) {
  new_spatial_fit(
    subclass       = "lm_fit",
    engine         = lm(price ~ elev, st_drop_geometry(train_sf)),
    formula        = price ~ elev,
    response_var   = "price",
    predictor_vars = "elev",
    data_sf        = train_sf
  )
}

# Required: cv_spatial() scores each fold through the predict() generic,
# which dispatches on the subclass named above.
predict.lm_fit <- function(object, newdata = NULL, ...) {
  if (is.null(newdata)) newdata <- object$data_sf
  as.numeric(stats::predict(object$engine, st_drop_geometry(newdata)))
}
registerS3method("predict", "lm_fit", predict.lm_fit)

# Required by summary() and model_metrics(): one value per training row.
fitted.lm_fit <- function(object, ...) as.numeric(stats::fitted(object$engine))
registerS3method("fitted", "lm_fit", fitted.lm_fit)

summary(lm_fit(site))
#> Summary of <lm_fit> fit (n = 80)
#> 
#>   Formula: price ~ elev
#> 
#>   In-sample metrics:
#>     RMSE    = 2.8624
#>     MAE     = 2.4374
#>     R^2     = 0.2622
#>     SMAPE   = 16.40%
cv <- cv_spatial(site, "price", "elev", fit_fn = lm_fit, k = 3, seed = 1)
#> cv_spatial(): no folds supplied -- using spatial block k-fold CV (k=3).
cv$overall
#>       RMSE      MAE     MAPE    SMAPE        R2 Adj_R2 n_pred n_MAPE n_SMAPE
#> 1 3.472328 3.009688 21.29953 20.27029 0.2341257     NA     80     80      80
# Check that these two agree before reading the metrics above.
c(attempted = cv$n_folds_attempted, succeeded = cv$n_folds_succeeded)
#> attempted succeeded 
#>         3         3
